business.title: A hierarchical resilient tri-level energy management for islanded multi-energy system with risk-aware learning-in-the-loop RL algorithm
business.desc: Coordinated energy management is crucial for the effective operation of integrated multi-energy systems (IMESs), which integrate water, heat, and electricity networks. The primary objectives of this coordination include reducing operational costs, minimizing hazards, and ensuring a reliable supply of energy. Traditional methodologies tend to address these objectives within a singular optimization framework, which often constrains their capacity to accommodate the distinct operational requirements associated with economic scheduling, vulnerability assessment, and service restoration. This study investigates the potential for enhancing system performance by dispersing these objectives into three interconnected decision-making tiers and coordinating their outputs throughout the operational phase. At the highest level, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is utilized to facilitate operational decisions that improve energy supply and service restoration during disruptions. The intermediate level employs a sensitivity-based risk assessment to pinpoint vulnerable system components and evaluate their effects on operational performance. At the foundational level, resources pertaining to power, heat, water, storage, and energy conversion are scheduled through Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP), which integrates resilience and risk outcomes as operational constraints and decision-making priorities. Furthermore, a Reinforcement Learning (RL) agent manages real-time operations by coordinating the outputs from these three levels, dynamically adjusting operational choices based on prevailing system conditions. This hierarchical flow of information enables resilience requirements and vulnerability assessments to inform economic scheduling without conflating all objectives into a single optimization problem. Simulations conducted on an IMES reveal that the proposed framework enhances energy supply during disruptions by 35.14% and reduces daily operating costs by 13.79% when compared to traditional benchmark approaches. These findings suggest that the proposed structure improves supply continuity and economic efficiency while effectively addressing operational vulnerabilities and network limitations.

business.title: Genome-wide association analysis and genomics-assisted prediction of seed productivity traits in Spinach (Spinacia oleracea L.)
business.desc: Understanding the genetic basis of reproductive traits can help improve spinach (Spinacia oleracea L.) seed productivity. We evaluated a diversity panel in Chimacum, Washington, during the 2023 season using genome-wide association analysis and genomic prediction. Analyses used 86,049 single-nucleotide polymorphisms, with 227 accessions for days to flowering and gender distribution and 195 for seed yield per female plant. The strongest associations were at SOVchr3_49591612, SOVchr2_3481334, and SOVchr3_1006345, with maximum − log₁₀(P) values of 11.95, 12.04, and 12.80, respectively. Positional candidates included SAP18 for flowering, a BURP domain-containing protein, and pollen-specific SF21 for yield, and a TPX2/importin domain-containing protein for gender distribution. Across 100 repeated holdouts, the highest reported mean predictive correlations were 0.636, 0.641, and 0.478 for the respective 20-, five-, and seven-marker panels. Because marker selection preceded resampling, these estimates describe predictive ability conditional on fixed panels rather than independent validation of marker discovery. Together, the associations, candidate annotations, and compact marker panels provide a focused framework for investigating reproductive timing, female seed productivity, and field gender balance, prioritizing genomic targets for fine mapping and marker validation in spinach breeding.

business.title: A benchmark for elevator fault diagnosis: Multi-level tasks from perception to diagnostic reasoning
business.desc: Elevator fault diagnosis is a safety-critical problem that requires capabilities beyond isolated fault classification, including knowledge grounding and structured reasoning for maintenance support. In this work, we present a benchmark for elevator fault diagnosis and organize evaluation into three complementary task groups: (A) sensor-based fault detection and classification, (B) taxonomy-grounded fault classification and cause identification, and (C) reasoning with incomplete or constrained information. To enable reproducible comparison across heterogeneous model families, we standardize task definitions, input/output formats, and scoring protocols and report component-level predictive metrics. Experiments across representative language models show task-dependent performance: higher performance on one task does not necessarily transfer to another. The benchmark is a reproducible testbed for studying diagnostic-assistance methods, not a validation of safe operational deployment.

business.title: Misinformation-based preventive behaviors during the COVID-19 pandemic in Myanmar: A cross-sectional study
business.desc: Widespread misinformation influenced public understanding of disease risk and preventive behaviors during the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly in low-resource and conflict-affected settings such as Myanmar. Although preventive behaviors were generally protective, some actions driven by misinformation may have been ineffective or harmful. Evidence on determinants of misinformation-based preventive behaviors remained limited. This study aimed to examine associations between misinformation-based preventive behaviors (MPB) and sociodemographic characteristics, information sources, social media use, and health belief factors in Myanmar. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among adults residing in Myanmar, with data collected between March and May 2024. Participants were asked to retrospectively report their preventive behaviors during the COVID-19 pandemic period (2020–2022). Data were collected using a structured questionnaire adapted from previous COVID-19 studies. The outcome variable was misinformation-based preventive behaviors, categorized as low (0–2 behaviors) and high (3–4 behaviors) engagement. Independent variables included sociodemographic characteristics, information sources, social media platform use, and selected health belief variables based on the Health Belief Model (HBM). A total of 434 respondents were included in the analysis, of whom 106 (24.4%) reported high engagement in MPB. Use of social media platforms other than Facebook was associated with higher engagement (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 2.30, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.22–4.35). Participants reporting ≤3 hours and 4–6 hours of daily social media use had lower odds of MPB engagement compared with those reporting >6 hours (AOR = 0.46, 95% CI: 0.25–0.86; AOR = 0.48, 95% CI: 0.24–0.95, respectively). Higher self-efficacy was independently associated with greater engagement in MPB (AOR = 1.70, 95% CI: 1.03–2.82). MPB were more strongly associated with information environments and specific health beliefs than with sociodemographic characteristics alone. These findings underscore the importance of addressing misinformation and improving access to reliable health information to reduce engagement in non–evidence-based practices.

business.title: Investigation on influence of lateral pressure coefficient of surrounding rock on drilling energy
business.desc: This study investigates the mechanism of drilling energy consumption under complex in-situ stress conditions. Drilling experiments were conducted on M15 mortar specimens under varying lateral pressure coefficients using a self-developed laboratory system. Results show that drilling velocity, rotation, and torque exhibit no clear regularity, while drilling work displays a “decrease–increase” V-shape trend centered at a coefficient of (1) A mechanical model of cutting under lateral pressure was established, indicating that drilling work is consistently higher than under isotropic pressure. The drilling work coefficient exhibits a piecewise functional relationship with the lateral pressure coefficient, with deviations up to 30% at a coefficient of (2) Experimental and theoretical results differ by 0.66%~8.76%. Unlike previous models assuming uniform confining pressure, this study reveals a nonlinear non-monotonic relationship between drilling work and lateral pressure coefficient (κ), and introduces a dimensionless coefficient (CE) to quantify the deviation from hydrostatic conditions. These findings provide a quantitative framework for drilling design and in-situ stress estimation. The results can be extended to vertical and inclined boreholes and are valuable for petroleum drilling, directional drilling, and in-situ stress measurement while drilling.

business.title: Minimizing data requirements for chemical and material property prediction via cluster-based training set selection
business.desc: Machine learning is increasingly used to predict chemical and material properties, and when data are scarce, data acquisition is often necessary to support these efforts. Despite the practical advantages of minimizing acquisition costs, it remains unclear which data acquisition strategies are the most efficient across diverse property prediction tasks or what principled basis underlies their relative performance. Here we survey 100 space-filling and active learning algorithms across 60 property prediction tasks, finding that cluster-based training set selection consistently outperforms active learning when choosing from a predefined candidate library, a result that runs counter to prevailing practice and is robust to the dimensionality of material representations, the choice of fixed or learned representations, and training set size. A theoretical framework grounded in Gaussian process variance establishes cluster-based selection as the principled optimum in the low-data limit, providing a unified basis for understanding training set quality across contexts. Overall, this work establishes cluster-based training set selection as a broadly effective and principled strategy for data-efficient, machine-learning-enabled materials design. A survey of 100 algorithms across 60 chemical and materials property prediction tasks finds that cluster-based selection of training data outperforms active learning, and a theoretical framework establishes why this occurs in the low-data limit.

business.title: Unified sliding-mode control of a flexible excitation system with lightweight stator/rotor dual-channel damping injection
business.desc: With the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources, power systems are increasingly exposed to broadband and strongly coupled disturbances. Under large disturbances, parameter perturbations, and operating-point variations, flexible excitation system (FES) may exhibit aggravated DC-link voltage fluctuations, sluggish excitation response, and insufficient damping of electromechanical oscillations. To address these issues, this paper proposes a unified sliding-mode control framework for a FES consisting of a three-level neutral-point-clamped voltage-source converter (NPC-VSC), a DC link, and a DC/DC excitation chopper. An adaptive-gain second-order sliding-mode (AG-SOSM) controller is introduced into the VSC outer loop to ensure finite-time convergence of the DC-link voltage and enhanced disturbance rejection. In the VSC current inner loop and the chopper control loop, band-pass-filter (BPF)-enhanced sliding surfaces are combined with the super-twisting algorithm (STA) to achieve fast tracking of the excitation variable with reduced chattering. In addition, lightweight stator-side reactive power damping and rotor-side damping-torque components are injected through the reference path, enabling coordinated dual-channel damping enhancement without modifying the main controller structure. Time-domain simulation results under network disturbances, mechanical-power perturbation, excitation-related parameter variations, and converter-current harmonic evaluation show that, compared with CES, PID-FES, and CSMC-FES benchmarks, the proposed strategy improves electromechanical damping, accelerates dynamic recovery, maintains DC-link voltage regulation, and reduces converter-current harmonic distortion.

business.title: TRIM31 aggravated cerebral ischemic injury by inhibiting autophagosome-lysosome fusion through degradation of TLR9
business.desc: Recent evidence has suggested that dysfunction of the autophagy-lysosome system was a crucial factor leading to neuronal damage, yet the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. Studies have reported that Toll like receptor 9 (TLR9) is required for autophagic flux. In our investigation, we observed that TLR9 was significantly upregulated and exerted a protective role through promoting the fusion of autophagosomes and lysosomes in the stroke models. Mechanistically, we found that tripartite motif-containing protein 31 (TRIM31) interacted with TLR9 and promoted the k48-linked polyubiquitination of TLR9, consequently facilitated its degradation in a proteasome-dependent pathway. Furthermore, TRIM31 led to impaired autophagosome-lysosome fusion in cerebral ischemic injury by negatively regulating TLR9. In conclusion, we identified TRIM31 as a novel E3 ubiquitin ligase for TLR9 degradation and provided a new therapeutic strategy to alleviate ischemic brain injury by enhancing autophagosome-lysosome fusion via TLR9.

business.title: Corrosion and corrosion fatigue studies of PBF-EB/M-manufactured porous iron in simulated body fluid
business.desc: One of the biggest limitations for the use of iron in biodegradable implant material applications is its slow corrosion rate and stress shielding. This research, therefore, focuses on the potential of increasing the corrosion rate and reducing the stiffness by tailoring the porosity of the substrates. The materials were prepared using powder bed fusion-electron beam melting, which allows for a high adjustment of porosity. The corrosion behavior was revealed via electrochemical impedance spectroscopy with modified simulated body fluid as an electrolyte over an immersion time of up to 48 h. Additionally, the corrosion products were investigated with Raman spectroscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy to reveal details of the corrosion mechanism. Corrosion rates were increased with higher porosity, and a critical pore size was found to be necessary to sustain accelerated corrosion and avoid the blockage of pores with corrosion products. The fatigue studies illustrate the relevance of pores, leading to a reduced fatigue lifetime of the powder bed fusion-electron beam melting Fe samples under corrosive conditions, which can be explained by both stress concentrations at defect sites and enhanced corrosion rates.

business.desc: When a CEO departs unexpectedly, boards have little time to find a leader who can steady the business, reassure stakeholders, and keep operations moving. Yet the person best suited to lead the company over the long term may not be the right choice to step in immediately.
